correctness.rationale: The two 7-component multiplicity vectors have exact message-weight profiles (4t+4,4t+4,4t+2,4t+6,4t+2,4t+2,4t+4) and (4t+4,4t+4,4t+4,4t+6,4t+2,4t+2,4t+2). The first minimum-weight triple has XOR zero, the second nonzero, so an invertible relabeling cannot map them precisely. Bijectivity forces one light-to-heavy and one heavy-to-light image, giving distortion at least [(4t+4)/(4t+2)]^2. Identity message map has exactly reciprocal extreme ratios, attaining it. Both matrices are full rank even at t=0. An actual standalone finite checker verified weight vectors and enumerated all 168 invertible maps for seven sample t values; finite checking is ancillary to the all-t proof.

value.rationale: The sharp all-length formula supplies a natural parameterized metric-geometry benchmark for the newly defined code-distortion invariant on the first dimension in which the seven nonzero messages have projectively distinct dependency patterns. It proves a concrete structural mechanism by which identical ordinary weight spectra conceal non-equivalence while optimal distortion decreases quantitatively to one, and finds a closed-form optimizer for an infinite family rather than an arbitrary small numerical test. It claims no general code-distortion optimum or algorithmic complexity advance.
